lines: I typed hello, and it says [jr;;p|J, R, semicolon, semicolon, P].
Put your fingers on your keyboard. Feel those tiny bumps on F and J?
Those little ridges are there for a reason.
And no, it's not a factory mistake, genius.
And today... I'm deleting them! Both of them!
Now try typing without looking. Your hands land one key too far to the right.
You wanted to write hello. You wrote [jr;;p|J, R, semicolon, semicolon, P].
Congratulations. You now type like a confused pigeon.
Those bumps mark the home row. Your left index finger goes on F. Your right index finger goes on J.
From there, every other finger knows exactly where its keys are. That's called touch typing.
That's how people type really fast, without ever looking down.
Meanwhile you're out here hunting for the letter Q like it owes you money.
And there's one more. The five on the number pad has a bump too, so your fingers find the middle.
So if you've been typing with two fingers your whole life... I'm not mad.
Those bumps are tiny. But they make you fast. Feel them right now.
So... what should I delete next?
